text:
jin: quick sync — planning decision for attention kernel chooser for next deploy. goal: v2/v3 switching based on input shape + kv behavior. want to lock heuristics by Fri.

olivia: +1. what are the heuristics? sequence length, batch size, kv-page usage?

jin: proposed set:
- prefer FAv3 for seq>=1024 or when kv_paged=false
- prefer FAv2 for seq<1024 when batch_size>16
- fallback to fused kernel for small seq small batch (latency win)

ashley: ran perf matrix on prod-like traces. short summary:
```
model: redwood-13b
workload: chat-short
metrics: p50 p95 tokens/sec
FAv3 seq<512: +8% p50 latency vs FAv2
FAv3 seq>=1024: -22% latency
KV paged=true: memory pressure + cache thrash on FAv3
```
link: https://perf.internal/reports/2134

marco: KV note — paged KV returns partial pages for long contexts, we should disable FAv3 when kv_page_fault_rate > 0.03

olivia: how do we measure page_fault_rate in runtime? metric name?

marco: runtime exposes `kv.page_fault_rate` per model/route. also `kv.cache_hit_ratio`.

perf-bot: regression alert (trial cluster): 2026-02-14 08:12 UTC — FAv3 rollout 10% showed p95 spike on small seqs

ashley: saw that — root cause: batching heuristic bundled short chats into larger micro-batches that increased context switching. patch: add `max_batch_for_short_seq=8`

jin: propose feature flags:
```
flags:
  attn.kernelchooser.version: adaptive-v1
  attn.kernelchooser.params:
    seq_threshold: 1024
    short_seq_batch_limit: 8
    disable_fav3_if_kv_paged: true
```

olivia: rollout plan?

jin: staged: 1% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 7 days with rollback triggers:
- p95 latency increase > 12% over baseline for 2h
- error rate > 0.5% above baseline
- kv.page_fault_rate increase > 0.02 absolute

ashley: perf dashboards and eval harness ready. will pin a smoke prompt set and run nightly.

marco: ops: add an alert to routing to redirect to FAv2 if page_fault_rate > 0.05

devops-bot: canary scheduled: Tue 2026-02-17 00:30 UTC (1% traffic) by jin

olivia: ok, I'll own metric tracking and slack updates. jin, can you open a short RFC with the chooser logic? :thumbsup:

jin: will do, drafting now, link when ready. thanks team :)
